text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: Paging: API Gateway error rate spike detected: 502/504 increase across edge proxies in eu-west-1 starting ~2m ago. Top symptoms: short bursts of 502s from edge, sustained 504s from api-gateway downstream. Trigger: 5xx rate > 3% over baseline for 2m. Pager: dana (oncall).

Dana: Acknowledged. I'm on call. Initial check: console dashboard shows total 5xx at 3.8% for the last 2m, but latency p50 steady. Looks localized to eu-west-1. Reproducing quick checks.

Rohit: I'm up. I'm seeing a fanout from edge->api-gateway->model-proxy with increasing queue depths on api-gateway pods. Could be a cascade from a single backend slow path.

Jules: Support reports 6 support threads mentioning timeouts from EU, some mobile clients. Customer-impact estimate: ~2.7% of incoming requests failing user-visible (mostly chat and embeddings endpoints).

Dana: Good context. Running quick tail on edge NGINX error logs.

Dana: ```
# tail -n 200 /var/log/nginx/edge-access.log | grep -E " 502 | 504 " | head
172.19.12.45 - - [15/Mar/2026:10:03:21 +0000] "POST /v1/generate" 502 0 "-" "redwood-sdk/1.2"
172.19.14.21 - - [15/Mar/2026:10:03:22 +0000] "POST /v1/embeddings" 504 0 "-" "curl/7.86"
```

Rohit: Checking api-gateway pods: increased goroutine count, outgoing latency to model-proxy spiking. Logs show intermittent TLS handshake timeouts to some model-proxy instances. Could be underlying host network flapping or NAT gateway exhaustion in the EU subnet.

sre-bot: Host network health in eu-west-1: minor packet loss detected on two ASGs (asg-model-proxy-2/3) over last 5m; cloud provider reports transient control-plane maintenance in the region.

Dana: Ok, that aligns. Immediate mitigation options: 1) divert eu-west traffic to eu-central and us-west (regional fallback policy) for non-legal/jurisdictional customers, 2) enable short-term rate-limit at edge for chat/embeddings to reduce fanout, 3) scale up api-gateway/model-proxy pools in eu-west if capacity available, 4) trigger circuit-breaker to fail fast to cached model variants. Thoughts?

Jules: For customer-impact minimization, fallback routing + quick rate-limit seems best. Some enterprise customers are geo-locked, need to check allowlist before shifting.

Dana: I'll start routing rule to shift 40% of non-enterprise EU traffic to eu-central via runbook, and apply a conservative 20rps per-key soft rate-limit for embeddings endpoint to reduce backend strain. Doing now.

Dana: ```
# apply routing override
POST /internal/route-override
{ "source_region": "eu-west-1", "target_region": "eu-central-1", "percentage": 40, "match": "!enterprise" }
# edge config applied
```

Rohit: Scaling api-gateway and model-proxy ASGs now: +2 instances each (if capacity available), spinning up warmed instances. Also putting affected model-proxy nodes into drain to isolate flappers.

sre-bot: Autoscale events: api-gateway-eu increased desired from 6 -> 8, model-proxy-eu 10 -> 12. New instances pending.

Dana: Applying soft rate limit rule for embeddings: ```
EDGE_RULE: path:/v1/embeddings rate:20rps per-key soft:true 503_on_exceed:false
```

Kevin: Adding quick cache hit amplification: bump prefix-KV cache TTL for embeddings to 45s for common embeddings keys to reduce compute. Pushing small config change to cache tier now.

support-bot: Notifying customers: support team queued a templated in-app banner for affected EU customers, stating degraded performance and mitigation in progress.

Dana: Quick health check after routing + rate-limit + scale (2m after): overall 5xx down to 1.1%, edge 502 spikes reduced, but some 504s persist from long-tail requests to legacy model variants. Latency p99 for a subset still elevated.

Rohit: Observed TLS handshakes recovered on most model-proxy hosts after draining/flapping nodes; remaining 504s seem correlated with a single older model variant (quantized-v0.9) that times out under the new routing mix. Plan: blacklist quantized-v0.9 for eu-west traffic and shift to quantized-v1.1.

Dana: Proceed with variant blacklisting for eu-west and add automatic fallback to quantized-v1.1. We'll make the change for non-enterprise traffic first.

Dana: ```
# block model variant
PATCH /internal/model-routing
{ "region": "eu-west-1", "blocked_variants": ["quantized-v0.9"] }
```

Jules: Customer impact update: support saw failed requests drop from 2.7% -> 0.6% for EU customers; enterprise customers on geo-lock still impacted at ~3% — will require manual contact.

Nora: Taking over oncall in ~10m. Dana, can you summarize remaining TODOs for handoff?

Dana: Handoff summary: 1) Monitor eu-west 5xx and p99 latency for 30m, 2) Confirm new instances join healthy pool, 3) Validate model-variant blacklist holds and no regressions on quality, 4) Work with infra to confirm cloud provider control-plane issues cleared, 5) Postmortem + customer comms owner needed (assign to eng-runtime + support).

Nora: I got it. I'll be on until resolved. If 5xx > 1.5% again, I will escalate and re-open routing. Also will contact two impacted enterprise customers for visibility.

Dana: Thanks. I'll start a short incident ticket and assign prelimsev/priority, capturing timeline and mitigation steps.

Dana: ```
INCIDENT (temp): IN-17550 - eu-west-1 edge 502/504 spike
Severity: Sev2
Impact: ~2-3% of requests, partial customer impact in EU, some enterprise customers geo-locked
Mitigations: regional fallback (40% non-enterprise), soft rate-limits on embeddings, scale up api-gateway/model-proxy, blacklist quantized-v0.9
Owners: dana (initial), nora (oncall handoff), rohit (runtime infra)
```

Rohit: I'll follow up with infra for cloud provider report and check instance network metrics (NAT port utilization) and share findings in the thread.

sre-bot: New instances are healthy and registered in LB pools. Network packet loss trending down.

Nora: Quick follow-up after 20m: 5xx stable at 0.4%, p99 latency trending to baseline. Enterprise customers still at ~1.8% due to geo-lock; support opened manual cases and we reached out to two customers.

Jules: Recommendation for postmortem: triage root cause between provider-side transient maintenance vs our NAT/connection reuse; add mitigations: more aggressive connection reuse and pre-warming, better model-variant circuit-breakers, and extend regional fallback automation.

Dana: Agreed. I'll draft postmortem and add action items: (A) increase NAT port pool for eu subnets, (B) add canary for model-variant timeouts, (C) automate enterprise-safe fallback opt-in/out, (D) create runbook step for quick edge rate-limits.

Nora: Closing note: Incident declared resolved at +45m. We'll convert this thread to a postmortem and assign. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
